sources: Kelly, Fergus. A Guide to Early Irish Law. Dublin: School of Celtic Studies, Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, 1988. Early Irish Law Series, Vol. III, pp. 3-4.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tuath is an ancient Irish concept. The word meant both a people and the land they lived on. Most people stayed within the bounds of their own tuath for their whole lives. They met friends, relations, and enemies at festivals and assemblies called oenach. Legal rights mostly held only within the tuath. The bard or poet, however, could travel beyond its borders. Each tuath chose its own king, and Ireland held many such groups. A king's power came from his tuath, his people and their land, and from his link with the goddess who stood for the territory.

okr.objective: Record the ancient Irish concept of the tuath.
